John the Baptist

precepts.text: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing. And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, heard I saying. There are creatures in heaven, creatures on the earth, creatures created deep inside the earth nobody has ever seen, and creatures in the sea like leviathan that no man has seen. And they all heard, and they understood. The creatures understand us; remember the donkey talked to Balaam and asked him, why are you beating me?
precepts.point: But the redeemed shall walk there, and the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads. That is us walking back into our land.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the wilderness and the desert shall be glad and “blossom as the rose.” When we are delivered, the desert places in our land will blossom and trees will start springing up, because we are connected to the earth. When the righteous people start ruling, everything changes. The animals are free, and the creatures understand us. That may sound like church talk, but the donkey did talk to Balaam: why are you beating me? Revelation shows how far that understanding goes.

“Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.” Christ receives all these things.

“And every creature which is in heaven”: those are the angels. There are creatures in heaven. “and on the earth”: the animals created on the earth. “and under the earth”: creatures created in the earth, worms and such, and creatures living deep in the earth that nobody has ever seen. “and such as are in the sea”: leviathan, and creatures in the sea no human being has ever seen, that the Lord created. “and all that are in them”: everything that was created.

“heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever.” They heard what John said, and they understood it, all the creatures.

That is why the land itself rejoices in Isaiah 35. The whole creation answers to the Lord, and when “the glory of Lebanon” is given and they “see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of our God”, it is because the Lord will be on the earth, and everything will change.

precepts.text: Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees: build up the spiritually weak brothers in every school, the inner circle and the trustworthy circle outside it. Say to them that are of a fearful heart, be strong, fear not; God hath not given us the spirit of fear. Behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence, a requital; he will come and save you. Isaiah 47:3 again: thy nakedness shall be uncovered by the word of God, and I will not meet thee as a man.
precepts.point: Some of you took the bag from the white man to sit up here in purple and report back. You have your house and car now, but the Most High has special destruction for sellouts and traitors, worse than the heathen's: weeping and gnashing of teeth, pain after death. Nowhere in the scriptures is there anything good for a traitor.

note.label: America: Hammer of the Earth

precepts.why:
David prays, “raise me up, that I may requite them”: raise me up the third day, so I can get vengeance on the traitor who ate of my bread. Isaiah tells the faithful to hold on for that vengeance: “Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.”

In every IUIC school some brothers may be weak and feeble, spiritually. Build them up. You have to build your inner circle up, loyal and faithful brothers who know the scriptures and fear God, and then have a circle outside of that of trustworthy, loyal men, so that when Jacob's trouble comes you don't all fall.

“Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not”. Brothers and sisters, be strong, because at times you might get afraid, but the Lord has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

Then: “behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” We must believe that our God will come with vengeance. A recompence is a requital, the same word as “that I may requite them” in the psalm: an appropriate return for wrongdoing.

Isaiah 47 shows that vengeance on Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen”. All these fake Christians talking about America being a Christian society: their nakedness is uncovered by the word of God, and all their shameful deeds are revealed. “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” Christ is not coming back meeting them as a man. So strengthen the weak, fear not, and wait on the God who comes with recompence to save us.

precepts.text: Your God will come with vengeance; he will come and save you.
precepts.point: It is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you, when the Lord Jesus is revealed in flaming fire taking vengeance on them that obey not the gospel.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
Paul thanks God “because that your faith groweth exceedingly, and the charity of every one of you all toward each other aboundeth.” That is what the body needs: brothers and sisters charitable toward each other, with that charity abounding, “in all your persecutions and tribulations that ye endure.” We will suffer for the kingdom of God, and in the suffering we still have to maintain love for our neighbor. It is not about one man; it is about the body of Christ.

Then: “Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you.” The ones troubling the apostles in Thessalonica were Rome. And the Lord Jesus shall be revealed “in flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Christ is coming back for vengeance. That was never taught in church, but it has been in the Bible all along.

Isaiah says the same thing in the Old: “Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” Be strong and do not fear; your God is coming back with vengeance and with the recompense we just read in Thessalonians.

“He will come and save you”: not all people. He is coming to save the Israelites. He is not coming for Christians, not for the Baptists, not for any denomination. And the vengeance falls on those who obey not the gospel, like our people who keep repeating the same evil every year, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year’s, knowing these things are not of God.

precepts.text: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped, and the tongue of the dumb sing.
precepts.point: Christ answers by pointing to the works: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. He is quoting Isaiah back to them.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

precepts.why:
John sends to ask if he is the one, and Christ answers by pointing to the works: “The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.” He is quoting Isaiah back to them.

Isaiah: “Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you. Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing”. The blind seeing, the deaf hearing, the lame leaping: these are the signs Isaiah gave of the day your God comes to save you. John knew the prophet, so the answer told him what he asked: the works Isaiah wrote of are being done, and the one Isaiah wrote of is here.
